speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: A strong Singapore Armed Forces (SAF) safeguards Singapore’s security, Independence and sovereignty.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: Without security and stability, we cannot achieve economic or social progress.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: However, the security landscape Singapore faces today is more complex.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: Many countries in our region are modernising their militaries against a backdrop of rising nationalism, unresolved maritime and territorial disputes, and persistent threats from terrorists and cyberattacks.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: Intensifying United States (US)-China competition, uncertainties in the Korean Peninsula, greater contestation in the waters and airspace around Singapore, and the continuing threat of terrorism, can potentially disrupt the peace and stability of our region.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: But just as potent are unexpected events that can change the status quo.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: The wider array of security challenges has placed more demands on SAF, even as our manpower pool shrinks.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: Defence spending will also have to take into account a mature economy with slower projected growth in the future and other needs from an ageing society and infrastructure spending.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: We can approach these challenges with confidence as steady investments in defence over the years have built a strong SAF that is able to deal with a broad spectrum of threats.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: More importantly, Singaporeans are united in their resolve and support to maintain a strong military and Total Defence.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: We recognise that new threat scenarios have evolved.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: Less advanced militaries and even non-state actors can now acquire sophisticated technologies and weaponry that used to be the domain of professional militaries.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: Through both physical and virtual threats in cyberspace, attackers have more avenues to disrupt and destabilise Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: In response, SAF will develop new fighting concepts and leverage technological advancements to increase our effectiveness and ensure more efficient use of manpower.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: For example, the Aerostat surveillance systems, Littoral Mission Vessels, and the Next-Generation Armoured Fighting Vehicles, supported by an advanced and secure communications network, have enabled SAF to be a tightly connected and flexible military force, capable of deterring the spectrum of potential aggressors.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: The Islamic State of Iraq and Syria (ISIS) and ISIS-inspired groups in our region are building up military-level capabilities and firepower, augmented by the return of battle-experienced fighters from the Middle East to our region.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: The siege of Marawi in 2017 was a key example, which required the joint efforts of the Philippines armed forces and its homeland security forces to dislodge militants from the city.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: SAF will work closely with the Home Team to ensure an effective and coordinated response to any terrorist threat.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: Exercises, such as NORTHSTAR and HIGHCREST, will be stepped up in scale and complexity to build interoperability.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: More SAF and Singapore Police Force servicemen will undergo joint security operations training at the SAF’s Island Defence Training Institute.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: We are also working with other countries under a “Resilience, Response, Recovery” framework to strengthen our responses to prevent, deal with, and recover from terrorist attacks in the region.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: As with kinetic defences, SAF will train and use qualified Full-Time National Servicemen (NSFs) and also grow its partnerships with local Institutes of Higher Learning to build a strong and capable cyber defence force.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: In 2017, Singapore celebrated the 50th anniversary of National Service (NS) and showed its overwhelming support for this vital strategic institution that ensures our survival.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: MINDEF and SAF will not take this support for granted.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: Instead, we will redouble our efforts to optimise the experience, contributions and potential of our NSmen.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: By making use of technology, SAF has reduced the physical demands of selected NS vocations, such as Security Troopers, allowing more servicemen to be deployed to vocations that they were previously ineligible for.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: MINDEF will also continue to take into consideration the interests of NSFs when assigning their vocations.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: This approach has allowed for more effective and meaningful deployment of our servicemen and encouraged them to take greater ownership of their NS roles and responsibilities.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: Singapore will continue to work closely with our neighbours and regional partners to enhance regional stability and address common security challenges.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: It is the highest defence consultative and cooperative mechanism in ASEAN.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: The ADMM-Plus was inaugurated in 2010 and includes the 10 ASEAN member states and eight Plus countries, namely, Australia, China, India, Japan, New Zealand, Republic of Korea, Russia and the US.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: As a small city-state, it is vital to shape an open and inclusive regional security architecture where the interests of all countries are protected.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: Platforms, such as the Shangri-La Dialogue, the ADMM-Plus Experts’ Working Groups, as well as the Five Power Defence Arrangements, all help to promote multilateralism and inclusiveness.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: SAF also contributes to international efforts to deal with transnational threats.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: SAF will also seek out more opportunities to train with the armed forces of Malaysia and Indonesia, to build stronger trust and people-to-people ties.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: Ultimately, Singaporeans are responsible for our own defence.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: Our strongest weapon against external forces is our unity and resolve to protect our way of life and keep Singapore independent and sovereign.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: No amount of tanks, planes or ships – no matter how sophisticated the systems we build – can make up for a divided nation.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: More than ever, Total Defence is needed and every Singaporean has to play his or her part to safeguard Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
text: Only together can we continue to keep Singapore safe and secure for another generation.
